# NNTP download-dialog results return through property-bag copy-back on unload

The header-download caller creates a writable property bag and reads hitOK/downloadAll after the modal dialog returns. The dialog works on a separate args object: load copies properties and sets cancel defaults, accept/cancel changes that object, and unload writes it back to the original bag. Preserve that copy-back boundary when changing this dialog; merely updating local args does not update the caller bag. No modal UI or runtime test ran.

Scope: NNTP modal download-header argument lifetime.
